title: DR scenario execution & terraform module notes (restore validation matrix)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is an operational playbook + module notes for executing disaster recovery (DR) restores for Private Deployments (VPC / on-prem). Focus: fast, testable restore procedures, terraform state recovery patterns, and a simple validation matrix engineers can run to assert service health and data correctness after a restore.

Audience:
- Platform engs running private deploys
- Solutions engineers helping customers recover
- Oncall SREs who may perform restores

Key objectives (high level):
- Clear, repeatable restore steps for common DR scenarios: single-region failure, full-site loss, accidental deletion, and failed upgrade rollback.
- Terraform module notes to make state recoverable and to avoid manual state gymnastics during restores.
- Small set of automated/hand-check validations (validation matrix) to confirm RTO/RPO targets met.

RTO/RPO targets (recommendation):
- Control plane (k8s control + API): RTO <= 2 hours for Dedicated Tier customers; RPO <= 15 minutes for critical metadata (if using WAL shipping).
- Data plane (model artifacts + KV caches): RTO <= 6 hours; RPO <= 1 hour for model registry syncs.
- Customer-specified sensitive data: align to contract (may be longer depending on airgap).

Snapshot strategy (summary):
- DBs: continuous WAL + hourly base snapshots. Store on two independent targets: on-prem object store and encrypted offsite blob (S3 compatible).
- Model artifacts: immutable versioned blobs (content-addressed) with daily replication to offsite.
- KV caches / ephemeral: rely on rehydrate from model predictions; include TTL mapping in config so behavior is predictable when missing.

Pre-restore checklist (quick):
- Confirm trigger: outage type (partial/total), confirm DNS change windows and customer SLAs.
- Identify latest good snapshot IDs (db, model-artifacts, object-store manifest, terraform state backup).
- Contact account owner + schedule maintenance window if needed.
- Ensure terraform remote state backend accessible (S3 endpoint or MinIO + state-locking).
- Lock Jira/Change ticket (JIRA-DR-1972) and assign roles.

Terraform module considerations and notes:
- Always enable remote state with locking. For on-prem we recommend MinIO (s3-compatible) + Consul for lock; variables: tf_state_bucket, tf_state_region (or endpoint), consul_addr.
- Keep a separate state namespace per customer (prefix: redwood/state/<customer-id>).
- Version modules explicitly (module sources pinned with tags). When making breaking changes to resource names add migration notes to module CHANGELOG, and a compatibility shim module for restores.
- Module outputs required for restores: cluster_id, kubeconfig_secret_path, db_snapshot_manifest, artifact_registry_prefix. Make these outputs stable between module versions.
- Include a lightweight helper module (tf helpers/restore) that can perform: state import for primary resources, recreate IAM/service accounts with minimal privileges, and write a skeletal state file that points to recovered resources.
- Store terraform state backups (at least 7 days rolling) as objects labeled with timestamp + sha of plan. Retain one weekly snapshot for 90 days.

Common restore scenarios (stepwise):
1) Accidental DB deletion (single cluster node failure):
  - Identify latest base snapshot id from snapshot manifests.
  - Restore DB into staging namespace (avoid overwriting prod) to run data integrity checks. Command example (postgres): pg_basebackup / restore s3://backups/customer/db/2024-10-20-base.tar.gz + replay WAL from s3://backups/customer/db/wal/
  - Run quick checks: row counts for key tables, sample query latencies, hash of migrations table.
  - If integrity OK, promote restored DB to primary via terraform tf/helpers/restore -> import new resource and update outputs.
  - Run validation matrix.

2) Full site loss (primary DC burned):
  - Bootstrap new infra in DR region using terraform: use tf helpers/restore to rehydrate state or import minimal resources.
  - Restore DB from most recent cross-site replicated snapshot.
  - Rehydrate object storage (model artifacts) from offsite blob store. For large tables use async background sync, but mark endpoints as degraded until sync completes.
  - Update DNS (short TTL required in pre-checks). Validate traffic flows to new region.
  - Post-restore: run full validation matrix + dry-run of a standard customer workload.

3) Failed upgrade caused schema drift or broken migrations:
  - Roll back to last known-good release using git tags + module pinning.
  - For DB: if migrations are destructive, restore DB snapshot just prior to upgrade. If forward-only migrations exist but are repeatable, consider writing a compensating migration.
  - Run data consistency checks.
  - Re-deploy with canary traffic and monitor schema-active alerts.

Restore validation matrix (run in order):
- Step A: infra smoke (SRE)
  - kube-apiserver responds to kubectl get nodes (expect all control plane nodes Ready).
  - Core system pods (dns, coredns, rbac-proxy) status=Running.
  - Expected: exit 0 on scripts/k8s-smoke.sh

- Step B: data integrity (DB team)
  - sample_query_checks.sh -> returns 0 and sample rows match previous checkpoint hashes.
  - migration_version table equals expected tag for rolled-back release.

- Step C: object store checks (artifact team)
  - manifest validation: head object for model vX returns 200 and checksum matches manifest.json
  - sample model pull: curl --fail <artifact-url>/vX/model.bin -> verify sha256

- Step D: end-to-end functional (product/solutions)
  - run smoke scenarios: generate a short prompt, embed a string, and run a rerank job. Compare outputs vs golden samples allowing nondeterminism thresholds.
  - throughput sanity: 95th percentile token latency < SLO for canary traffic.

- Step E: service-level verification (SRE + customer success)
  - make a test request over same network path as customer (VPC peering test) and validate headers, auth, and response codes.
  - check billing/usage counters for expected counters to be increasing.

Automation and scripts to keep in repo (suggested):
- scripts/terraform-state-fetch.sh -> downloads state backups, verifies checksums.
- scripts/restore-db-checks.sh -> runs sample queries and calculates hashes.
- scripts/restore-rehydrate-artifacts.sh -> parallel rsync/transfer from offsite.
- scripts/dr-exercise-runner -> small harness that drives the validation matrix and emits a short report.

Post-restore runbook (short):
- Notify stakeholders: email + Slack channel #dr-incident with brief status and next steps.
- Keep incident tape: store restore steps + evidence into ticket (JIRA-DR-1972).
- Schedule a 72-hour observational window: monitor for latent errors, performance regressions, and data drift.
- Plan a root-cause meeting and add improvements to backlog (tag: dr-incident).

Upgrade integration notes (how DR testing ties into upgrades):
- Every major module release must include a mandatory DR-scenario test in staging: perform a simulated restore from snapshots and run validation matrix.
- For infra changes that rename resources, include a migration plan and a tf/helpers/restore shim that can map old resource names to new ones during state recovery.
- Add a guarded terraform plan step that checks for destructive actions on production state and requires an approval gate before apply.

Unresolved questions / open items:
- RTO targets for airgapped customers who do not allow offsite replication (proposal: RTO <= 12 hours, document variation per-customer).
- Define standard retention for model artifacts vs customer contractual terms.
- Automating WAL replay verification to reduce manual checks.

Quick references / commands:
- List available snapshots: aws --endpoint-url https://minio.company.internal s3 ls s3://backups/customer/db/
- Download snapshot: aws --endpoint-url https://minio.company.internal s3 cp s3://backups/customer/db/2025-01-09-base.tar.gz /tmp/restore/
- Import restored resource into terraform: terraform import module.db.redwood_database "db-<restored-id>"
- Recreate kubeconfig secret from exported kubeconfig: kubectl create secret generic redwood-kubeconfig --from-file=kubeconfig=/tmp/kubeconfig -n redwood-system

Postscript: exercise cadence
- Quarterly DR tabletop + annual full restore run for high-tier private deployments. Runbook owners must sign off in product PRD before upgrade windows.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add exact checklist for Consul restore (KV + sessions)
- Add small grafana dashboard to show snapshot replication lag per-customer
- Wire up script dr-exercise-runner into CI for every module tag so tagging a release triggers a lightweight restore smoke in staging.

End of doc.
